articles.title: New Fantasy Football 2026 Mock Draft Tips and Latest Consensus Rankings
articles.summary: The final week of the 2026 NFL preseason is underway, and real, meaningful football is nearly back. For fantasy enthusiasts, this means that we are entering the prime drafting window.
articles.body:
The final week of the 2026 NFL preseason is underway, and real, meaningful football is nearly back. For fantasy enthusiasts, this means that we are entering the prime drafting window.

Drafting after the August 30 roster cuts will be ideal, as managers will then have a clearer idea of player roles and roster statuses. Between now and then, though, they can prepare for their live drafts by running a few mocks and collecting the data.

Of course, to get the most out of mock drafts, it's best to execute them with a purpose. Here, you'll find some mock-drafting tips, a three-round mock conducted with FantasyPros' Mock Draft Simulator , and a look at FantasyPros ' latest consensus point-per-reception (PPR) rankings.

The biggest piece of advice we can offer about mock drafting is to take notes, track data, and pay close attention to where your favorite players are being taken. This information can help you create a personalized draft board that is more beneficial than even the latest consensus rankings.

The trick is to make sure that your mock draft parameters—roster makeup, scoring rules, flex options, etc.—match your actual draft perfectly. Under those guidelines, you may find that certain players you have circled pre-draft are going higher or lower than their consensus average draft position (ADP) might suggest.

When creating a personalized draft board, it's also a good idea to track any sleepers you've identified and wish to target. Has that high-upside rookie RB drifted upward from Round 12 toward Round 9? That's great information to have on draft day and can help prevent missing out on a prospect you love.

Experiment With Different Strategies, but Focus on RBs Early or Zero RB

Managers should try mock drafting from different positions, even if they know their draft slot, in order to get a feel for how other drafters may approach things. They should also try out different strategies to identify a preferred approach and a strong Plan B.

Whether you want to target a high-volume receiver like Ja'Marr Chase early in Round 1 or have your heart set on two elite RBs, there's a good chance that other managers will make that plan difficult.

In 2026, there's going to be a massive drop-off in RB talent after the initial wave. Players like James Cook, De'Von Achane, and Chase Brown form a solid group just under the elites—high-volume backs like Jahmyr Gibbs and Bijan Robinson—but second-tier backs like Josh Jacobs and D'Andre Swift are far less appealing.

We'd recommend trying different strategies that yield at least one high-level RB within the first two rounds and two out of the first three. The WRs available in Rounds 4-8 are likely to have much more value than the RBs available in that range.

However, we'd also recommend trying a few zero-RB strategies as a backup plan. If there's an early run at the position, managers might benefit from snapping up top-tier WRs and TEs while looking for RB value after other starting lineups have been filled.

For example, getting RJ Harvey ( draft rank of 107) in Round 9 might yield far more value than taking Travis Etienne Jr. ( draft rank of 47) five rounds higher.

Lastly, it's important to run as many mock drafts as possible in order to get the most accurate collection of data.

Even one or two mocks can help managers get a feel for how they want to draft—and help get used to the panic of being on the clock right after your favorite player got sniped. However, a larger sample size will always paint a more accurate picture of where players are being valued and how strategies are working.

articles.title: Man who masqueraded as 49ers player facing federal charges in alleged wire fraud scheme that exploited women
articles.summary: He and another man are accused of defrauding at least 26 victims of more than $1.3 million, according to the U.S. Attorney's office in the District of Oregon...
articles.body:
A man who adopted "fictitious personas," one of which notably was that of a fake San Francisco 49ers player, is part of a duo that's been arrested and charged for defrauding several women of more than $1.3 million, according to the U.S. Attorney's office in the District of Oregon .

The FBI arrested 35-year-old Daejon Love and 18-year-old Taylor Jamie Chan on Monday in Boise, Idaho, where they were apprehended upon meeting at the Boise Airport. They're facing a pair of federal charges: conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud, as detailed in a statement released this week by the U.S. Attorney's office that references court documents.

Love, who the U.S. Attorney's office says repeatedly posed as a Niners player or as a wealthy real estate investor, and Chan, who the U.S. Attorney's office says acted as Love's financial adviser, allegedly accrued the aforementioned sum by exploiting at least 26 victims. Those are the ones the FBI has identified, and the bureau believes there are "many more."

The alleged scheme spanned four years, beginning in February 2022. Love and Chan targeted women in California, Oregon, Washington and Idaho, most of whom Love met through dating apps, prosecutors said. Love has used several names — including Jon Love, Daejon Love, Avril Lyto Love and Jordan Love — while carrying out the caper, per the U.S. Attorney's office.

"Love convinced many of the victims they were in sincere romantic relationships with Love, that he was a sophisticated investor, and that Chan was his investment adviser who helped Love grow a fortune worth tens of millions of dollars," the U.S. Attorney's Office statement said. "Love had romantic relationships with many of the victims and told them he wanted to build wealth and a future together. Love advertised nonexistent investment vehicles and claimed these investments would generate massive returns for both him and his victims."

"Love convinced many of the victims they were in sincere romantic relationships with Love, that he was a sophisticated investor, and that Chan was his investment adviser who helped Love grow a fortune worth tens of millions of dollars," the U.S. Attorney's Office statement said.

"Love had romantic relationships with many of the victims and told them he wanted to build wealth and a future together. Love advertised nonexistent investment vehicles and claimed these investments would generate massive returns for both him and his victims."

Phony bank and investment accounts and balances, created via phone applications, allegedly allowed Love to strengthen the validity of the ploy. Chan and Love even held three-way FaceTimes to flaunt falsified investment gains to whichever victim was on the call, according to the U.S. Attorney's office.

Victims sent Love and Chan money with the intent that it would be deployed for fruitful investments overseen by the tandem, prosecutors said.

"Once victims had no more money to invest, or if they asked too many questions, Love blocked communication with them but kept their money," the U.S. Attorney's office statement said.

"Of the victims identified and interviewed, none reported receiving any proceeds, returns on their principle, or investment account information, after sending Love and Chan money."

At the time of Love and Chan's arrest, Love was in Idaho to meet new victims, per investigators.

articles.title: Falcons QB Tua Tagovailoa booed by Dolphins fans as Miami pays price for failed relationship
articles.summary: Tua Tagovailoa completed 7 of 8 passes against his former team but still hasn't locked down the Atlanta Falcons starting job over Michael Penix Jr.
articles.body: As reunions go, Tua Tagovailoa’s return to South Florida as an Atlanta Falcon against his former Miami Dolphins teammates was not exactly a happy one. Dysfunctional is a better word for it. For six seasons, Tagovailoa and the Dolphins tried to make it work. They failed. DOLPHINS NOT GOING TO 'THROW IN THE TOWEL AND JUST REBUILD' BUT THAT COMES WITH HIGHER EXPECTATIONS Tagovailoa was set back by some coaches who didn’t like him and injuries that too often overshadowed him, so he never reached his goal of becoming the face of the franchise. And the Dolphins never came close to reaching the championship level they expected when they drafted Tagovailoa in the top five in 2020 and paid him like a top-five quarterback in 2024. The failures resulted in a divorce during the offseason and this exhibition game at Hard Rock Stadium was the first time the couple happened to be at the same place at the same time since the split. And guess what? Everybody believes they're better off after the separation. But no one is at this stage better off after the separation. DOLPHINS CONSULTANT TROY AIKMAN WILL BE LIMITED IN MNF ROLE LIKE RAIDERS MINORITY OWNER TOM BRADY IS ON FOX Tagovailoa is trying to earn a starting job with the Falcons and the fact he came into this game without yet having done so speaks to his failing since training camp began. Because Tagovailoa has basically been competing only against himself while Michael Penix Jr. has been limited in practices as he makes his way back from a 2025 knee surgery. And, yet, with his only significant competition sidelined and the path to the starting job clear, Tagovailoa hasn't been able to lock the job down. The Dolphins? They got rid of Tagovailoa this offseason despite the fact he would be costing them some $55 million in salary in 2026 alone. There's another bill coming next year. The Dolphins were so over this relationship they paid Tagovailoa to go away. And where has that left them? The Tagovailoa move was part of a systematic divestment from talent in order to "solve the salary cap problem" the previous administration got the franchise into. MIAMI DOLPHINS ENTER FULL REBUILD WITH MALIK WILLIS AT QUARTERBACK AND JEFF HAFLEY AS HEAD COACH The Dolphins are now perhaps the least talented team in the NFL as they prepare for a season in which they will be rebuilding for the 1,387th time in the past decade. So here we were on Friday night: Team Rebuild versus Quarterback Not Good Enough. The scene played out in front of a sparse crowd at Hard Rock that mustered enough emotion to boo for the quarterback they once believed would win them a championship. The Sadness Bowl. And, fittingly, nobody really won. Tagovailoa played well enough, completing 7 of 8 passes. But it wasn't actually good. The Dolphins, resting their talent-needy starting defense, fought with backups that will provide substandard depth this season. And the sparing between a QB who is lacking against backups who are lacking was, well, lacking. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Tagovailoa completed 3 of 4 passes on his first drive, with the only incompletion on a throwaway. The Falcons scored a touchdown that drive. But that last paragraph reads more impressively than it looked because the dynamic 43-yard completion from Tagovailoa to Kyle Pitts that highlighted the drive was actually a 4-yard pitch on a screen that the tight end turned into a big run against a scattered defense. On his second drive, Tagovailoa fumbled the snap from center and the Dolphins recovered. And another drive later, running back Brian Robinson fumbled and, once again, the Miami defense recovered. So, good on the Miami defense that is going to get steamrolled once the regular-season begins. And good on Tagovailoa, who still hasn’t done enough to win the Falcons’ starting quarterback job despite facing little healthy competition until this week, when Penix Jr. was fully cleared to practice. Good on both. But not really that good. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: New Seahawks owner Vinod Khosla defends Steelers fandom after saying he still watches all of their games
articles.summary: No one ask him about Super Bowl XL.
articles.body:
Vinod Khosla, the new owner of the Seattle Seahawks, might have a made the mistake of being too honest while introducing himself to his team's fanbase.

Speaking with reporters on Thursday, the day after the NFL's owners unanimously approved his $9.612 billion purchase of the Seahawks , Khosla discussed his past NFL fandom. Specifically, he confirmed he rooted for a team other than the Seahawks before buying them.

That team wasn't the San Francisco 49ers, whom Khosla purchased a 3% stake in alongside his son last year (which he will now be selling).

No, it's the Pittsburgh Steelers, the NFL's dominant team when Khosla entered the United States decades ago. He said still considers himself a fan of the team and watches every game:

"I happened to come to this country in '76 when the Steelers were winning Super Bowls, so actually I was originally, and still am, a big Steelers fan, also. Little known fact, but I still watch all the Steelers games too."

That one answer drew quite a bit of interest, so much so that Khosla decided to further explain himself on social media the next day. He insisted he will always want the Seahawks to win and complained about the media's reaction to his comments.

"Reporters will make every molehill into a mountain just to get column inches to write or video minutes. What's wrong with admitting my 1976-78 period in Pittsburgh (CMU) got me excited about the NFL? I still watch their games doesn't mean I won't unconditionally ALWAYS as owner, want the @Seahawks to win and have every edge up, EVERY TIME over every other team!!!! Zero questions!!! At the other end is a set of teams I always want to lose every advantage. But happy to have the sports writer getting more column inches and fill their pages. You are welcome. Apologies in advance for my very transparent style."

Khosla obviously wouldn't be the first person to have dual rooting interests in the NFL. We're just dealing with the rare owner who does not care if fans know he has another team he still loves. That's ultimately up to him, but you could forgive Seahawks fans for being a little more wary of what this era will look like.

Khosla's tenure as owner will ultimately be decided by the product on the field and the conduct of the organization. In the meantime, let's just hope he doesn't bring up Super Bowl XL too much in the Pacific Northwest.
